hypothesis: Down-weighting each net's cut probability by 1/log(1+k) (fan-out-aware cut weight) so huge clock/reset nets stop dominating the cut gradient and the objective instead optimises the many small-signal nets that carry most TNS violations.
analysis: (1) No — hypothesis not supported: total −3.4%, robust −2.1%, TNS −0.4%; down-weighting large nets did not improve small-signal TNS. (2) C3 drove the loss (score −2.4%, dWNS −4.3%) despite fewer cut/wcut nets (582→571, 1955→1926) and unchanged repair flips (353); critically, crit_cross rose 0.069→0.084, so fewer cuts but more critical-pair crossings — the mechanism backfired. C1/C2 essentially flat. (3) Seed spread is high (std 0.034; C3 per-seed −0.09 to +0.02), exceeding the mean effect — not acceptable. (4) Next: gate the 1/log(1+k) weight to non-critical nets only, or add a crit_cross penalty term, and re-run with more seeds.
